selected_test_names.description: The nominal maximum derives from floor((256-13)/6), not an independent test allowance. Every rendered selector still obeys sum(name bytes)+N+13 <= 256. No truncation or omitted witness.

native_oracle_preparation.description: The store-selected qualified preparation for an immutable job's exact readiness reference, never a latest-run guess or worker assertion. Pure-Go top-level tests only. The native owner proves exact pinned file bytes, cwd, build-selected nonempty witnesses, and compile-only readiness. Non-Go and resolved embed inputs must be declared pinned fixtures or explicit compiler inputs; no production Go/module replacement. Every stage pins the installed toolchain and native target with GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOPROXY=off, GOFLAGS=-mod=readonly, CGO_ENABLED=0, GOWORK=off, and a private disposable GOCACHE. No aggregate scratch quota or uncommitted-diagnostics promise. Preparation grants no worker attempt, verification authority, or semantic acceptance.

native_oracle_stream.description: Native producer descriptor only. One raw BLOB per stream stays on the existing verify lease. A complete ref requires atomic full capture; incomplete and abandoned output cannot supply full-output acceptance. Preview truncation does not imply stream truncation.

reference.description: A workflow reference list item with no Unicode White_Space characters and 2-128 UTF-8 bytes. Slashes are allowed because touched refs name repository paths.

domain_cards.description: Pinned repository_file references derived by the shared reader. The group supplies the validated Domain identity. Cards also occupy the existing required_reading bound; content is never inlined.

subject_ref.description: The author's claim about what the finding concerns; never dispatch-owned subject identity.

domain_id.description: A current Domain of the Product registry, validated against the registry and the approved affected scope at admission.

product_wide_rationale.description: Required exactly when domain_id names the registry's root Domain; a child Domain never carries one.

finding_id.description: Core-derived from the source event sequence and ordinal; never authored.

kind.description: The generic claim vocabulary of an authored finding. A ranked oracle finding projects the empty kind: its identity is the oracle tie, never a generic claim class.

evidence_refs.description: The evidence that supports the finding. A ranked finding without an oracle tie projects null; the core reader owns that wire shape.

status.description: A finding is a reported claim, never acceptance. The open status names a ranked review finding the lineage currently holds open: still a claim, and open.

source_kind.description: Present only on a ranked review finding: the entry carries an oracle tie and rides the open-set lineage, never the generic worker-claim notebook.

oracle.description: The typed oracle tie of a ranked review finding: classification plus the owner, predicate/law, case, and control references that bind it.

domain_id.description: A current Domain of the Product registry, validated against the registry and the approved affected scope at admission.

product_wide_rationale.description: Required exactly when domain_id names the registry's root Domain; a child Domain never carries one.

path.description: A normalized relative repository-contained path. Absolute paths, traversal segments, and a leading tmp segment refuse: the context never requires a tmp source.

source_event_frontier.description: The work item's maximum event sequence at read time, so a packet built from this view can be compared against current state before spawn.

entry_point.description: The named entry path or transition this case exercises.

expected_state.description: A bounded description of the expected state, never a new predicate DSL.

recipe_source.description: The exact pinned recipe manifest, not the candidate's modified harness. argv.description: The exact argument vector, never shell text.

expected_result.description: The declared exit-status result the harness must produce. Slice A admits pass (exit 0) only.

required_evidence_role.description: The evidence role the control's receipt must carry.

readiness_evidence_refs.description: The qualified native preparation run references for this exact owner/case/control bundle, parent contract, Project, raw subject, and environment. worker_oracle_finding.description: The typed oracle tie of one review finding: a closed classification plus the owner, predicate/law, case, and control references that bind it. Classification and severity are different dimensions; the tie records no acceptance.

classification.description: delivery_blocker: a failed obligation of a declared owner. uncovered_case: a legitimate new entry path the inventory omitted — a real blocker, not a rejection. follow_up: outside the approved owner/contract; never an open repair criterion. oracle_defect: the harness itself is obsolete, inconsistent, or unsound; it blocks readiness, not a fabricated repair.

entry_point.description: For an uncovered_case: the explicit new entry path or transition the inventory omitted.

continues_finding_id.description: The earlier ranked finding of this work that this finding continues. Same failure, same canonical open identity; an uncertain join becomes a new finding and earns no shrink credit.

variant_of.description: The owner-family finding this newly reproduced alternate entry path is a variant of. A variant is a new identity, not the same open finding.

worker_oracle_law_binding.description: One pinned law revision that explains an owner's obligation, plus the clause or criterion it serves.

report_protocol.description: Dispatch-owned final-report framing, covered by the authorized packet digest. New builders pin this protocol; absence identifies historical legacy output. This is not report schema or worker identity.

context.description: Prose context a packet built before the typed record members carried. The lane-packet schema keeps it so a retained packet from an attempt dispatched before that change still validates on recovery. The core dispatch admission refuses it, so no new packet carries it.

law_context.description: The approved contract's binding law and Domains the pinned continuity resolved. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet member differs from the current recorded state, omits a present record, or carries a member no record backs.

design_record.description: The current typed design record (CD-0128). The core refuses a dispatch whose packet member differs from the current recorded state, omits a present record, or carries a member no record backs.

proposal_record.description: The recorded proposal's problem, user outcomes, and constraints. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet member differs from the current recorded state, omits a present record, or carries a member no record backs.

work_context.description: The current work-context view the work pin carried when the packet was built, including the selected research entries it resolved. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet does not consume the current view byte-for-byte.

checkpoint.description: The latest context checkpoint the pinned continuity projection carried when the packet was built. The core refuses a dispatch whose packet does not carry the latest checkpoint byte-for-byte.

worker_packet_checks_repair_job.description: The selected worker-job revision this attempt executes on a repair-capable pin (CD-0205 D4). It carries the same full job shape as $defs/worker_packet_worker_job, including the optional core-recorded checks_repair metadata, under a distinct name so the frozen decoder's packet3 closure keeps the byte-exact pre-repair job shape its pins replay. The core refuses a packet whose worker_job is not a ready or review-bound recorded revision with this exact content. inputs.task stays the complete parent contract premise; this object bounds the attempt's own objective.

acceptance_oracle.description: The owner-level acceptance oracle of this immutable revision. Optional and omitted on every revision a pre-oracle definition recorded; required by oracle-capable definition versions. It enters the job digest and reaches every admitted lane through this same copy.

worker_packet5_worker_job.description: The selected ready worker-job revision a packet5 attempt executes: the packet2/3 worker_job shape plus the optional core-recorded checks_repair metadata (CD-0205 D4), the recorded production-size members, and the dispatch-time caller exclusions (CD-0225 D1, CD-0227 D1). The core refuses a packet whose worker_job is not a ready or review-bound recorded revision with this exact content; the exclusions are the core's own computed set and bind the packet, never the job digest. inputs.task stays the complete parent contract premise; this object bounds the attempt's own objective.

acceptance_oracle.description: The owner-level acceptance oracle of this immutable revision. Optional and omitted on every revision a pre-oracle definition recorded; required by oracle-capable definition versions. It enters the job digest and reaches every admitted lane through this same copy.

production_size_max.description: The recorded production-size cap (CD-0225 D1). Optional and omitted on every read-only revision; carried beside the measurement basis by every editing revision.

measurement_basis.description: The recorded measurement basis of this revision: the immutable base commit and the classified path inventory. Optional and omitted on every read-only revision.

direct_caller_allowance.description: The recorded conditional direct-caller scope of this revision (CD-0227 D1). Optional and omitted on every read-only revision.

caller_exclusions.description: The measured paths of the work's other jobs currently in correction. The core computes this set at dispatch admission and refuses a packet whose exclusions differ; the member binds the packet, never the job digest, and only the implementation capability class carries it.

worker_job_split.description: The closed split variant of record_worker_job (CD-0225 D3): one atomic record that replaces the current predecessor revision with two or more new successor jobs under the predecessor's cap, with an evidenced allocation of the predecessor's measured paths. The store checks reference coverage and exact retained content, not prose equivalence.

predecessor.description: The predecessor's current recorded revision, named exactly by job_id, revision, and digest.

job_id.description: A workflow reference list item with no Unicode White_Space characters and 2-128 UTF-8 bytes. Slashes are allowed because touched refs name repository paths.

successors.description: The successor jobs, each a new job_id recorded at revision 1 with the ordinary job content.

allocation.description: The evidenced allocation of the predecessor's measured paths to successors. Every predecessor inventory path is allocated.

worker_job_split_allocation.description: One allocation entry: the successor that owns the listed predecessor paths and the evidence for the assignment.

job_id.description: A workflow reference list item with no Unicode White_Space characters and 2-128 UTF-8 bytes. Slashes are allowed because touched refs name repository paths.

paths.description: Normalized relative repository paths, each inside the named successor's path_scope.

worker_job_split_successor.description: One successor job's content: the ordinary record_worker_job members. Its revision, Project scope, contract version, and digest are core-derived exactly as for an ordinary recording.

job_id.description: A workflow reference list item with no Unicode White_Space characters and 2-128 UTF-8 bytes. Slashes are allowed because touched refs name repository paths.

objective.description: The store counts this field's length in UTF-8 bytes: x-maxBytes and x-minBytes carry the enforcing byte bounds, and the code-point minLength/maxLength are derived from them so they never refuse a core-admitted string.

stopping_condition.description: The store counts this field's length in UTF-8 bytes: x-maxBytes and x-minBytes carry the enforcing byte bounds, and the code-point minLength/maxLength are derived from them so they never refuse a core-admitted string.

reserved_integration.description: The store counts this field's length in UTF-8 bytes: x-maxBytes and x-minBytes carry the enforcing byte bounds, and the code-point minLength/maxLength are derived from them so they never refuse a core-admitted string.

replaced_attempt.description: The exact completed overrun attempt this split replaces. Supplemental classifications serve only its overrun evidence; they change no inventory or descendant authority.
